claims.cytotoxic_mechanism: At 2.5 uM, PHA-665752 is expected to be largely inactive because it is a potent but non-cytotoxic ATP-competitive c-Met inhibitor whose antiproliferative effects require oncogenic MET addiction and typically manifest only at higher concentrations or with prolonged exposure.
